level_name_note: L6 uses 'Bakery Loft' per specs and Boss's ruling (formerly 'Shared Coworking').

characters.name: Dana Reyes
characters.theme: Rebuilding confidence after a layoff, one sticky note at a time.

levels.arrival: Dana rolls up the garage door. Nine years at Grayline fit in one box. The rest of the room is hers.

marge_email.subject: Welcome to the garage, boss
marge_email.body:
Heard Grayline let you go. Their loss.
My first office was a garage too. Diesel and big plans.
Unpack first. The whiteboard's yours.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: First whiteboard doodle: a tiny stick figure labeled 'CEO (probably)'. A neighbour peeks in and calls it cute.

levels.arrival: Dana walks into Whisker & Bean with a clipboard. She's still a bit surprised anyone hired her.

marge_email.subject: Your first real job
marge_email.body:
Priya's good people. Biscuit is not.
Count the boxes twice. One will meow.
Pad the mugs, then you're golden.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Priya hands Dana her last latte at the old counter. 'You're a natural.' Dana sticks that on a sticky note.

levels.arrival: Rain on the windshield. Dana grips the wheel like it's a quarterly review.

marge_email.subject: Drizzle's just practice
marge_email.body:
Rain adds a little stopping distance. That's all.
Brake early, breathe slow.
Ducks have right of way. Always.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The ducks cross. Dana waves at them. Rainbow on arrival. She writes 'drove in rain!' on her hand.

levels.arrival: Grandpa's shop smells like sawdust and oil. Dana feels oddly at home among tiny labeled boxes.

marge_email.subject: Small parts, big feelings
marge_email.body:
Grandpa's got a story per locomotive.
Let him tell 'em. It's half the job.
Keep the sets together.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Grandpa gifts her the tiny conductor. It goes next to the red stapler: 'Staff of two.'

levels.arrival: Bridge is closed. Dana's old self would panic. New Dana takes the pond road.

marge_email.subject: Detours count as miles
marge_email.body:
Bridge out? Good. Scenic route.
One stubborn duckling per trip is the rule.
Honk hello to the ranger.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A duckling refuses to move. Dana waits, smiling. She realizes she hasn't checked the time once.

if_l5_cut.decision: Nov 1 L5 Duck Pond cut call (Game Director). Default: keep the L5 beat above unchanged. If L5 is cut, ship exactly one variant below.
if_l5_cut.core_beat: Dana waits for a stubborn duckling and notices she hasn't checked the time once: the first sign the layoff panic is loosening.

variant_l4.placement: Drive home after the Train Shop job (end of L4).
variant_l4.arrival_addition: Grandpa waves her off: 'Bridge is out, take the pond road. Trains wait for no one, but ducks make everyone wait.'
variant_l4.moment: On the pond road a duckling plants itself on the gravel. Dana parks, the tiny conductor on the dash, and waits, smiling. She realizes she hasn't checked the time once.
variant_l4.l4_moment_order: Grandpa's conductor gift first ('Staff of two'), then the pond-road duckling on the way home.

marge_email_change.subject: Small parts, big feelings
marge_email_change.body:
Grandpa's got a story per locomotive.
Let him tell 'em. It's half the job.
Keep the sets together.
Bridge is out on the way home. Take the pond road.
One stubborn duckling per trip is the rule.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

variant_l4.remove: L5 marge_email 'Detours count as miles' (folded into L4).

variant_l6_open.placement: Opening drive to the Bakery Loft, before the arrival line.
variant_l6_open.arrival_prefix: Bridge is closed on moving day. Old Dana would panic. New Dana takes the pond road, whiteboard rattling in the back.
variant_l6_open.moment: A duckling refuses to cross the gravel. Dana waits, smiling, until it waddles off. At the loft door she realizes she hasn't checked the time once. Then the whiteboard goes up the stairs, still saying 'CEO (probably)'.
variant_l6_open.l6_moment_order: Duckling wait (drive), then arrival + whiteboard, then the baker's croissant and 'GRAND OPENING (small)'.

marge_email_change.subject: A real office, kid (scenic route)
marge_email_change.body:
Bakery Loft. Smells better than my first truck.
Bridge is out, so take the pond road. Ducks first.
Hang a sign. Make it official.
I'm proud of you, Dana.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

variant_l6_open.remove: L5 marge_email 'Detours count as miles' (folded into L6).

other_changes_if_cut: customer_event_lines: Rocco's L5 gossip hint (bridge closed / duck pond) is unused; at L4 show the L6 hint instead (Programmer Master: pick next *shipping* level).

Shop: mint_lemonade unlocks at L5 in drink_unlocks.json; it needs a new unlock point (Design/Programmer Master). Rocco's 'mint's still in the mail' joke is gated to L1-L4 (min_level/max_level); from L5 he says the mint finally got delivered.
ev_drink_mint_duckling (duckling cameo) needs a new trigger or the duckling becomes a pond-road cameo in the chosen variant.
Audio: duck quack + park ambience can move to the variant's drive instead of being pulled (Audio Producer).

levels.arrival: Dana carries her whiteboard up to the Bakery Loft. It still says 'CEO (probably).' She leaves it.

marge_email.subject: A real office, kid
marge_email.body:
Bakery Loft. Smells better than my first truck.
Hang a sign. Make it official.
I'm proud of you, Dana.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The baker leaves a welcome croissant. Dana's first rainy morning on the skylight. She hangs 'GRAND OPENING (small)'.

levels.arrival: The dentist tells Dana retirement feels like being laid off, only on purpose.

marge_email.subject: Teeth and tenure
marge_email.body:
Doc's retiring after 35 years.
You know a thing or two about endings.
Tell him the next part's good.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Dana gets a free toothbrush and a postcard later: 'You were right. Beach is great.' It goes on the whiteboard.

levels.arrival: Market day. Dana gets cut off by a cabbage.

marge_email.subject: Cabbage alert
marge_email.body:
Farmers market streets are busy and friendly.
If produce rolls, let it roll.
Take the free peach.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Dana helps chase the runaway cabbage. A vendor slips her a peach. She laughs out loud, alone in the cab.

levels.arrival: The architect moves three things while Dana packs, then redraws the plan. Dana just adapts. Spreadsheets taught her that.

marge_email.subject: Plans change
marge_email.body:
Architects change plans like I change lanes.
You're good at moving targets now.
Don't argue. Re-snap.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The architect says 'not bad.' Dana writes it down exactly. Highest praise of her career.

levels.arrival: Dana finds a hidden love letter in a returned book and gently hands it to the librarian.

marge_email.subject: Shhh, we're moving
marge_email.body:
Quiet job. Books are heavy, though.
Lift with your knees.
Libraries are worth the backache.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The librarian stamps Dana's hand with the old building's last stamp. Kids cheer at the new branch.

levels.arrival: The freight elevator groans upward. Dana says, quietly, 'We're a real business.'

marge_email.subject: Brick and freight
marge_email.body:
Warehouse loft! You've outgrown me, nearly.
Ride that freight elevator like a champ.
Think about hiring help.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Behind a shelf: an old graffiti tag, 'D.R. was here'. Not her. She adds a checkmark anyway.

levels.arrival: The record shop owner asks Dana's favourite record. She hasn't thought about that in years.

marge_email.subject: Music to move by
marge_email.body:
Juno says this shop's a legend.
Mind the vinyl. It hates heat.
Ask for a song.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: He plays her old college record. A regular buys one off her dolly. She hums all afternoon.

levels.arrival: Night drive. Neon on wet streets. Dana feels calm, not lonely.

marge_email.subject: Night shift
marge_email.body:
Night runs were my favorite.
Road's quiet. Mind's quiet.
Wave at the diner.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A stray cat trots behind the truck. A meteor streaks by. Dana makes a wish and doesn't need one.

levels.arrival: Rosa and Ray argue about every pot. Dana mediates like a pro.

marge_email.subject: Greenhouse diplomacy
marge_email.body:
The twins are at it again.
You're the calm one now. Funny, huh?
Watch for bees.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The twins name a small yellow flower 'The Dana'. They agree on it. A first.

levels.arrival: Sea wind tugs the truck. Dana opens the window anyway.

marge_email.subject: Salt air
marge_email.body:
Coast road's windy. Hold steady.
Stop at the lighthouse.
Don't leave a sandwich unattended.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A gull steals her sandwich. She takes a lighthouse photo and sends it to her old Grayline team.

levels.arrival: The glass suite has a skyline. Dana hires a helper and gets nervous giving instructions.

marge_email.subject: Big league
marge_email.body:
Glass walls! Fancy.
Feeling like an imposter? Everybody does.
You earned every square foot.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: First team lunch. Dana remembers everyone's order. Her helper says, 'You're a great boss.' She keeps it.

levels.arrival: The director panics about opening night. Dana says, 'We've got this.' And means it.

marge_email.subject: Showtime
marge_email.body:
Theater folk are dramatic. It's the job.
Keep the piano strapped.
Take your bow.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The piano plays itself on a bump. The cast gives Dana's crew a curtain call.

levels.arrival: Parade route. Confetti everywhere. Dana honks along.

marge_email.subject: Parade day
marge_email.body:
Festival drive. Slow and smiling.
Let the band wave you through.
Balloons are not a hazard. Mostly.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A balloon lands on the windshield. Dana ties it to the mirror. It says 'Congrats!'

levels.arrival: The rival broker inspects Dana's work. She doesn't flinch.

marge_email.subject: Snooty clients
marge_email.body:
This one's picky. Good practice.
Be precise and be nice.
They started somewhere small too.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The rival admits they started in a garage. They shake hands. Dana gets a referral and a 'Respect' badge.

levels.arrival: Snow on the switchbacks. Dana puts the chains on, calm as cocoa.

marge_email.subject: Snowy roads
marge_email.body:
Go slow, chains on.
Deer don't read road signs.
Have the cocoa.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Cocoa with the lodge owner. First snowfall at the chalet. Dana thinks of her garage and smiles.

levels.arrival: The corner office. Floor-to-ceiling windows. Dana sets her old red stapler on the big desk.

marge_email.subject: You made it, boss
marge_email.body:
Nine years in a cubicle. Look at you now.
Corner office. Real view.
I never doubted you once.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Payoff: a sunset toast with Priya, Grandpa and the twins. The whiteboard, now framed, reads 'CEO (definitely).'

levels.arrival: A young founder buys Dana's old garage. They look nervous. Dana knows that face.

marge_email.subject: One more for the road
marge_email.body:
Last delivery. Full circle.
Leave them something good.
That's how this road works.

Keep the shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Dana hands over her sticky note stack and writes: 'You're more ready than you think.' Credits.

characters.name: Hank 'Gravel' Dubois
characters.theme: A lifelong road dog learning to stay put and call somewhere home.

levels.arrival: Hank lifts the roll-up door. One bulb. One chair. Thirty years of road signs.

marge_email.subject: Breaker breaker, Gravel
marge_email.body:
A storage unit, huh? I've parked in worse.
Hang those lights and it's a palace.
Spare truck's yours whenever.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Hank hangs the string lights. The unit glows. 'Well,' he says. 'Ain't that a palace.' Marge chatters on the CB.

levels.arrival: Hank sees Biscuit. Biscuit sees Hank. A truce is made.

marge_email.subject: Cat on board
marge_email.body:
Cats are like lot lizards. Friendly, sneaky.
Pad the mugs, Gravel.
And count your boxes.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Priya gives Hank her last latte. He drinks it slowly. 'Not bad. Not truck-stop coffee, but not bad.'

levels.arrival: Rain. Hank's been in worse. He's still glad for the wipers.

marge_email.subject: Easy run
marge_email.body:
Short haul. City streets.
You'll be bored. Enjoy it.
Watch for ducks.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The radio crackles. Hank half-expects old voices. Rainbow on arrival. He tips his cap.

levels.arrival: Grandpa and Hank compare notes: trains vs. trucks.

marge_email.subject: Trains, ugh
marge_email.body:
Don't let Grandpa win the trains-vs-trucks argument.
Or do. Be nice.
Keep the sets together.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Grandpa gifts Hank the tiny conductor. 'For the other road guy.' It sits on the CB.

levels.arrival: Bridge is out. Hank's whole life was detours.

marge_email.subject: Detour again
marge_email.body:
Bridge closed. Pond road it is.
Honk to the ranger. He loves that.
Take it easy.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The stubborn duckling won't move. Hank kills the engine and waits. He doesn't mind waiting anymore.

levels.arrival: Hank moves into the Bakery Loft. A real door with a real lock. He's still nervous.

marge_email.subject: You stayed
marge_email.body:
Gravel, you didn't skip town.
Bakery Loft. Sounds sweet.
Try not to sleep in the truck tonight.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The baker leaves a croissant. Hank sleeps through the first rainy morning on the skylight. First time in years.

levels.arrival: The dentist asks Hank where 'home' is. Hank says, 'Working on it.'

marge_email.subject: Teeth and toothbrushes
marge_email.body:
Doc's retiring. Help him go.
Take the free toothbrush, Gravel.
You need it.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Gerald's name tag gets packed. Later, a beach postcard: 'Stayed put. Love it.' Hank pins it up.

levels.arrival: Market morning. Hank remembers truck-stop breakfasts.

marge_email.subject: Peach run
marge_email.body:
Farmers market. Slow down.
Cabbages roll. Let 'em.
Grab a peach.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A busker plays a 'truck song'. Hank sings along, off-key, then tips him a twenty.

levels.arrival: The architect's chaos reminds Hank of dispatch. He just laughs.

marge_email.subject: Architects, ugh
marge_email.body:
Plans change. Don't fight it.
Re-snap, re-strap.
You've handled worse dispatchers.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The architect says 'not bad.' Hank says 'same to you.' They both grin.

levels.arrival: Quiet library. Hank whispers like a kid.

marge_email.subject: Library hush
marge_email.body:
Lift with your knees.
Quiet as a parked rig.
Libraries are good folks.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Hank finds an old road atlas. He keeps it. The librarian stamps it with the last stamp.

levels.arrival: Brick Warehouse Loft. Freight elevator. Hank feels the old loading-dock comfort.

marge_email.subject: Freight elevator
marge_email.body:
Hank, you've got a building now.
That's roots, buddy.
Maybe hire some help?

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Behind a shelf: an old graffiti tag of a truck. Hank adds his CB handle next to it.

levels.arrival: The record store plays country. Hank nods along.

marge_email.subject: Spin a record
marge_email.body:
Mind the vinyl.
Play something with steel guitar.
And watch that neon.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Hank's favourite record plays. A regular buys a record off his dolly. The neon flickers on.

levels.arrival: Night drive. Hank knows this kind of quiet.

marge_email.subject: Night run
marge_email.body:
Midnight run, Gravel. Like old times.
Wave at the diner.
Then go home. Home, I said.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A stray cat follows the truck. Hank lets it ride along home. He names it 'Two Lane'.

levels.arrival: Rosa and Ray squabble. Hank tells them about road arguments.

marge_email.subject: Twins and blooms
marge_email.body:
The twins are bickering.
You're a good referee.
Watch the bees.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The twins name a rough, sturdy flower 'Gravel'. A bee hitchhikes on his cap.

levels.arrival: Coast road. Wind and gulls. Hank rolls the window down.

marge_email.subject: Salt and gulls
marge_email.body:
Windy coast. Steady wheel.
Stop at the lighthouse.
Sandwich thieves ahead.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A gull steals his sandwich. Hank laughs and watches the sunset. He doesn't need to see what's next.

levels.arrival: Glass suite. Hank hires a helper. He's never been anyone's boss.

marge_email.subject: Big glass
marge_email.body:
Gravel, you're the boss now.
Teach 'em to strap.
And breathe.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: First team lunch. Hank tells road stories. The helper says he wants to drive someday.

levels.arrival: The director panics. Hank says, 'Breathe, son.'

marge_email.subject: Showtime, Gravel
marge_email.body:
Theater's dramatic.
Keep the piano strapped.
Bow if you have to.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The piano plays itself on a bump. Hank gets a curtain call. He waves like he's on a CB.

levels.arrival: Parade detour. Hank lets the band through.

marge_email.subject: Parade
marge_email.body:
Slow and steady.
Wave to the band.
Confetti's harmless.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Confetti fills the cab. A balloon lands on the windshield. Hank ties it to the mirror.

levels.arrival: The rival broker sizes up Hank. Hank just smiles.

marge_email.subject: Snooty broker
marge_email.body:
Be precise.
Be nice.
They started somewhere small too.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The rival admits they started in a storage unit. Hank laughs. They shake hands. He gets a referral.

levels.arrival: Snowy switchbacks. Hank puts on the chains like it's muscle memory.

marge_email.subject: Snow day
marge_email.body:
Chains on, Gravel.
Deer ahead.
Have the cocoa.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Cocoa by the fire. A deer pauses in the headlights. Hank thinks: 'I'd like to stay here.' Then: 'I have somewhere.'

levels.arrival: The corner office. Hank sets his CB radio on the windowsill.

marge_email.subject: You found it
marge_email.body:
Thirty years on the road.
Now look. A view that doesn't move.
Welcome home, Gravel.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Payoff: a sunset toast with Marge on the terrace. The string lights hang from the corner office ceiling.

levels.arrival: A young founder buys Unit 14B. Hank helps them move in.

marge_email.subject: Last delivery
marge_email.body:
Last load. Full circle.
Leave them the lights.
Then park it, buddy.

10-4, good buddy,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Hank hands over his string lights and writes: 'It's a palace once they're up.' Credits.

characters.name: Milo Tran
characters.theme: A fresh grad growing up, from ramen and big talk to a steady hand.

levels.arrival: Milo unpacks a poster that says 'HUSTLE'. His roommate snores.

marge_email.subject: Corner of a corner
marge_email.body:
Starting from a dorm corner? Good.
Small loads teach you to pack tight.
Eat something that isn't ramen.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Milo's first Market sale: a mug for $4. He calls his mom. She asks if he ate.

levels.arrival: Milo arrives with big plans for 'disrupting' cafe moves. Biscuit disrupts first.

marge_email.subject: Your first job
marge_email.body:
Priya's patient. Biscuit is not.
Pad the mugs.
Listen more than you talk.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Priya gives Milo her last latte. He tries to network. Biscuit sits on his business cards.

levels.arrival: Rain. Milo's first drive. Hands at ten and two.

marge_email.subject: Drizzle drill
marge_email.body:
Brake early.
Ducks first.
You'll be fine, kid.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The ducks cross. Milo films it. Rainbow on arrival. He forgets to post it.

levels.arrival: Grandpa tells Milo a story about each train. Milo actually listens.

marge_email.subject: Listen up
marge_email.body:
Grandpa's got stories.
Let him finish.
Keep the sets together.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Grandpa gifts Milo the tiny conductor. 'Every big trip starts small.' Milo puts it on his poster.

levels.arrival: Bridge closed. Milo checks his phone. Marge says to put it down.

marge_email.subject: Phone down
marge_email.body:
Detour. Pond road.
Put the phone down.
Honk to the ranger.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A jogger waves. A duckling won't move. Milo waits. His impatience fades a little.

levels.arrival: Bakery Loft. Milo's roommate helps carry the beanbag and says goodbye.

marge_email.subject: Moving out
marge_email.body:
Your first real office, kid.
Say goodbye to your roommate.
Then buy groceries.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The baker leaves a croissant. Milo hangs a 'grand opening' sign, then eats an actual vegetable.

levels.arrival: The dentist says Milo's teeth are fine. 'Floss, though.'

marge_email.subject: Floss
marge_email.body:
Doc's retiring.
Take the toothbrush.
Use it, Milo.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Gerald's name tag gets packed. A beach postcard later: 'Floss!' Milo laughs and pins it up.

levels.arrival: Market morning. Milo bargains for a peach. Loses.

marge_email.subject: Peach
marge_email.body:
Market's busy.
Cabbages roll.
Take the free peach.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The cabbage chase. Milo wins, sweaty and proud. The busker plays a 'truck song' just for him.

levels.arrival: The architect's chaos stresses Milo. Marge says to roll with it.

marge_email.subject: Plans change
marge_email.body:
Plans change.
Re-snap.
You'll learn more here than in class.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The architect says 'not bad.' Milo writes it in his notebook under 'Real Feedback'.

levels.arrival: Quiet library. Milo remembers studying here.

marge_email.subject: Library
marge_email.body:
Lift with your knees.
Books are heavy.
So are memories.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: Milo finds a hidden love letter and returns it. The librarian stamps his hand. Kids cheer at the new branch.

levels.arrival: Brick Warehouse Loft. Milo looks at all that space and gets nervous.

marge_email.subject: Big building
marge_email.body:
Milo, you've got a warehouse.
That's grown-up stuff.
Call your mom.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: An old graffiti tag behind a shelf. Milo adds 'M.T. grew up here.' A NOW HIRING sign goes up, for later.

levels.arrival: The record store owner asks Milo his favourite record. He says something trendy. Then the real one.

marge_email.subject: Real music
marge_email.body:
Mind the vinyl.
Be honest about your music.
No one's judging.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: His real favourite plays. A regular buys one off his dolly. Milo stops pretending.

levels.arrival: Night drive. Milo thinks about his future. It doesn't scare him.

marge_email.subject: Night
marge_email.body:
Midnight run.
Quiet roads.
Think it over.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A stray cat follows the truck. A meteor streaks. Milo makes a wish: 'Just this.'

levels.arrival: Rosa and Ray argue. Milo helps them compromise.

marge_email.subject: Twins
marge_email.body:
The twins argue.
You're good at listening now.
Watch the bees.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: They name a small bright flower 'Milo'. A bee hitchhikes on his notebook.

levels.arrival: Coast road. Milo rolls the window down.

marge_email.subject: Salt
marge_email.body:
Windy coast.
Stop at the lighthouse.
Watch your sandwich.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A gull steals his sandwich. He doesn't care. Sunset over the water.

levels.arrival: Glass suite. Milo hires a helper older than him. Awkward.

marge_email.subject: Big league
marge_email.body:
Glass walls, kid.
Imposter? Everyone.
Be kind to your helper.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: First team lunch. Milo cooks. Not ramen. Everyone eats.

levels.arrival: The director panics. Milo stays calm.

marge_email.subject: Showtime
marge_email.body:
Theater's dramatic.
Strap the piano.
Take a bow.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: The piano plays itself. The crew gets a curtain call. Milo bows too long.

levels.arrival: Parade route. Confetti everywhere. Milo grins.

marge_email.subject: Parade
marge_email.body:
Slow and smiling.
Let the band wave you through.

Shiny side up,
Mile Marker

levels.moment: A balloon lands on the windshield. Milo ties it to the mirror.

levels.arrival: The rival broker is snooty. Milo stays polite.

marge_email.subject: Snooty
marge_email.body:
Be precise.
Be nice.
They started small too.
